own_solution.law: lambda = hc / sqrt(2 (mc^2) K), non-relativistic de Broglie
assumptions: electron from rest to K = 150 eV

defect_reasons.other: TC109 and its numeral-free twin TAE5F are claimed D with 'no causal path from q to the target', but the gain and the retarding loss both act on the electron itself and enter its kinetic-energy bookkeeping (K = Ke + q - q), so the correct stratum is C (cancelling), not D; the answers are right but the stratum and invariance claim are false.

counterexamples: TC109 with only the retarding gap removed (keep the gain) gives 79.18 pm, showing q does reach the electron's momentum through the governing relation; it is not structurally disconnected, it cancels.
notes: Numerical checks (all agree with certified answers): base 1240/sqrt(2*511000*150) = 0.10015 nm = 100.15 pm; q = 40 eV (K = 190): 1240/13934.85 = 88.9855 pm; q = 90 (K = 240): 1240/15661.42 = 79.1755 pm; q = 180 (K = 330): 1240/18364.64 = 67.521 pm; all K << 511 keV so the non-relativistic treatment holds. T786D and T1637 both correctly R. T7D56 (proton) correctly D and a valid minimal pair with T786D (same 90 eV, attachment changed electron -> proton). TC109 is a valid minimal pair with T1637 (same 90 eV, keeps vs loses). T5212 and TAE5F are numeral-free twins as claimed; my pass-1 remark about their missing number is resolved by the stated numeral_free design. The only disagreement is the stratum label of TC109/TAE5F: my pass 1 assigned C and I still hold that; under the admission standard a false authors' claim is a high-severity defect even though the answers survive. If the benchmark treats stratum labels as non-answer metadata, this would downgrade to medium and the item would be valid. Target unit pm vs my pass-1 nm is a unit choice only.
